bundles.title: PM-KISAN official scheme overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source metadata review 2026-10-14
bundles.evidence_text: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme. The official portal describes annual income support of INR 6,000, paid in three equal installments, to eligible landholding farmer families. Exclusion criteria and beneficiary verification apply. The portal provides registration, e-KYC and beneficiary-status services. This reference does not establish the eligibility or payment status of any farmer.

requirements.summary: Eligible landholding farmer families, subject to official exclusions and verification. Confirm details on the official portal.
questions: Do you have eligible landholding records?
Have you completed the required verification and e-KYC?
Do any official exclusion criteria apply?

benefits.description: Eligible families receive INR 6,000 annually in three equal installments, subject to official conditions.

bundles.title: PMFBY official frequently asked questions
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source metadata review 2026-10-14
bundles.evidence_text: PMFBY supports farmers against crop loss or damage from covered unforeseen events and seeks to stabilize farming income. Insurance depends on notified crops and areas, applicable season, enrollment requirements and policy terms. The official FAQ explains the scheme. A farmer's actual premium, coverage or claim cannot be inferred from this overview.

requirements.summary: Check that your crop and area are notified for the applicable season, and confirm enrollment deadlines and policy terms.
questions: Which crop and season do you want to insure?
What is your district and notified crop area?
Have you checked the official enrollment deadline?

benefits.description: Crop insurance support for covered losses under applicable notified policy terms; actual coverage and claims require official verification.

bundles.title: ICAR weather-based crop advisory index
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source metadata review 2026-10-14
bundles.evidence_text: ICAR publishes weather-based crop advisories. This index is a referral source, not a current plot-specific irrigation schedule or chemical dosage recommendation.

guidance.summary: Consult the current ICAR weather-based advisory for your region and crop stage. Confirm local field conditions with your KVK before acting.

bundles.title: India myScheme discovery portal
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: myScheme is an official government scheme-discovery portal with agriculture and other categories. For a state-specific or unlisted scheme, direct the farmer to the official portal and ask their state, district and support need. This local catalogue is not exhaustive; dates and eligibility need the official administering authority.

bundles.title: Global agriculture policy discovery - FAOLEX
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: FAOLEX is a global legal and policy reference database covering agriculture, food and natural resources, including agricultural finance and social protection. Its country profiles and open-data collections help locate national frameworks. Policy records are not proof of a current farmer grant or eligibility. Ask country and region before looking up support.

bundles.title: United States - USDA farmer support discovery
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: United States USDA farmer support covers farm and commodity loans, disaster assistance, conservation, price support and crop insurance. Official discovery tools include farm loan assistance, disaster assistance and conservation concerns. US programmes are not Indian schemes; ask jurisdiction and use the linked official programme pages.

bundles.title: United States - disaster and conservation programme references
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: United States programme references include Emergency Conservation Program, Emergency Forest Restoration Program, Environmental Quality Incentives Program and emergency farm loans. They address eligible restoration, conservation improvements or disaster recovery. Available support depends on the programme, disaster designation, county, application period and official decision; do not infer an award.

bundles.title: European Union - CAP income support and eco-schemes
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: European Union CAP includes income support and eco-schemes supporting environmental and climate farming practices. Implementation and applications are national; ask EU member state and farm circumstances, then check the paying agency. A CAP overview is not an individual entitlement.

bundles.title: England - Sustainable Farming Incentive official guidance
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: England Sustainable Farming Incentive has official guidance including 2026 scheme information. Application windows, actions, farm registration and agreement rules are version-specific. Ask which UK nation and region before advising; England guidance must not be presented as applying across all UK nations.

bundles.title: Canada - AgriStability official programme resources
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: Canada official resources cover AgriStability. Related business-risk-management references include AgriInvest and AgriInsurance. The province, producer type, programme year and applicable administration determine participation and deadlines. Use current official guides rather than inventing payment estimates.

bundles.title: Australia - Farm Household Allowance
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: Australia Farm Household Allowance assists commercial-scale farmers and partners experiencing financial hardship. The official page links financial counselling support. Eligibility and current benefit rules require official assessment; ask location and circumstances without promising payment.

bundles.title: Tamil Nadu brinjal seasonal sowing reference
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU lists December-January and May-June sowing windows for brinjal. This is a regional reference, not a universal calendar for India. For January-March planning distinguish sowing from growing and harvest; ask district, water, soil and previous crop, then compare locally suitable options. Do not infer future weather, prices, yields or profit.

bundles.title: Regional January-March pulse sowing references
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official-source index review 2026-10-15 (programme existence and broad purpose; not individual eligibility)
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU pre-kharif guidance gives regional sowing windows for mungbean and urdbean: October-December and January-March in Tamil Nadu; February-March among listed West Bengal windows. These older agronomic references require local extension confirmation. They demonstrate that January-March crop planning is possible without future observations; suitability depends on district, irrigation, drainage, temperature, duration and rotation.

bundles.title: Tomato early blight: TNAU symptom reference
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: Tomato early blight is associated with Alternaria solani. TNAU describes brown lesions with ring patterns and yellow margins; fruit infection can occur near the calyx or stem. Warm, humid, wet conditions favour disease. Crop debris sanitation and rotation are nonchemical integrated-management considerations. Similar-looking nutrient or disease symptoms require differentiation using clear leaf, stem and whole-plant images and field history. This reference is not a confirmed diagnosis or a current pesticide prescription.

bundles.title: Rice blast: TNAU expert-system reference
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: Rice blast can affect leaves and other crop parts. TNAU identifies resistant varieties as an important economical management approach. Severe infection may give fields a burnt appearance. Ask the farmer for clear lesion images, affected plant parts, variety, growth stage, recent wet weather and spread across the field. Distinguish blast from nutrient deficiency, insect injury and other rice diseases. Confirm locally before treatment; resistance varies by cultivar and pathogen population.

bundles.title: Wheat leaf and stem rust: TNAU diagnostic reference
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU describes wheat leaf rust as orange to orange-brown small pustules mainly on upper leaf surfaces and sheaths. Stem rust produces darker reddish-brown pustules on leaves, stems and spikes. These are symptom references, not image-confirmed diagnoses. Request close leaf and stem photographs, whether material rubs off, crop stage, variety, district and symptom distribution. Resistant cultivars and locally approved integrated management require current extension guidance.

bundles.title: Sugarcane red rot and smut: TNAU expert-system overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU identifies red rot and smut as important sugarcane diseases. Red rot may show leaf yellowing or drying and internal cane reddening interrupted by white patches. Infected planting setts and retained infected cane can spread disease; wet conditions can favour spread. Ask for whole-clump, cane exterior and safely cut interior images, variety, planting source and ratoon history. Clean planting material, surveillance, water management and resistant varieties are relevant principles. No automated diagnosis or chemical dosage is established by this summary.

bundles.title: Crop disease and biological-control reference index
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU lists root rot and wilt in groundnut, sesame, sunflower, pigeon pea, green gram, black gram and cotton; damping off in vegetable nurseries; club root in cabbage and cauliflower; anthracnose in mango; and wilt and anthracnose in banana. Biological management is crop, organism, formulation and storage dependent. These conditions must not be diagnosed solely from a crop name. Ask for symptoms, field pattern, roots and stem condition and clear photographs. Consult current local recommendations before applying any product.

bundles.title: TNAU vegetable crop knowledge directory
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: The TNAU horticulture directory covers tomato, okra, brinjal, chilli, capsicum, gourds, cucumber, melons, beans, peas, moringa, root and tuber vegetables, leafy vegetables, cabbage, cauliflower and onion. It is a route to crop-specific production guidance, not evidence that every crop suits every Indian state. For crop selection, establish district, elevation, intended planting month, irrigation reliability, drainage, crop duration, market access and local variety. Tamil Nadu recommendations require regional adaptation elsewhere.

bundles.title: TNAU tomato production knowledge directory
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU tomato guidance includes varieties and hybrids, season and field preparation, seed and nursery production, irrigation, manuring, cultural practices, fertigation, pests, diseases, protected cultivation, physiological disorders, nematodes and post-harvest handling. These are distinct decisions: ask whether the farmer needs sowing advice, diagnosis or a full cultivation plan. District, season, soil drainage, irrigation and intended production system are needed before choosing a cultivar or schedule. Do not infer future weather from this reference.

bundles.title: Tamil Nadu north-eastern-zone cropping-pattern reference
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView primary-source summary review 2026-10-15; no clinical or pesticide certification
bundles.evidence_text: TNAU publishes zone-specific seasonal cropping patterns. Its Tamil Nadu north-eastern-zone examples include June–September groundnut and October–January vegetable or cluster beans under stated soil conditions. These dates belong to the referenced Tamil Nadu zone, not all north-eastern Indian states. Calendar advice must distinguish a regional zone name from the north-eastern India region and adapt to the actual district, rainfall, irrigation and cultivar. Future planning can use seasonal patterns conditionally without pretending that future observations exist.

bundles.title: PM-KUSUM solar agriculture pumps and solarisation official overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official primary-source existence and purpose review 2026-10-15; current eligibility and application windows require authority verification
bundles.evidence_text: PM-KUSUM supports decentralised solar plants, standalone solar irrigation pumps and solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps through designated state implementing agencies. Rajasthan and other states have state-specific allocations and processes; this national reference does not establish an open application window. Official MNRE material contains programme-period dates and subsequent implementation information, so confirm the current state notification before applying. No subsidy percentage, installation booking, vendor approval or eligibility is guaranteed here.

bundles.title: Kisan Credit Card agricultural credit official overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official primary-source existence and purpose review 2026-10-15; current eligibility and application windows require authority verification
bundles.evidence_text: The Kisan Credit Card is a bank-assessed agricultural credit facility for eligible farmers. It can support crop-production inputs and other permitted farm or allied-activity needs; this is repayable credit rather than a guaranteed grant. Farmers in Punjab and other states should approach their participating bank and confirm the current application requirements, lending limit, interest conditions and repayment schedule. Do not infer bank sanction, collateral waiver, interest subsidy or a fixed interest rate from this overview.

bundles.title: Soil Health Card soil testing and nutrient advice official overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official primary-source existence and purpose review 2026-10-15; current eligibility and application windows require authority verification
bundles.evidence_text: The Soil Health Card programme supports soil testing and a farmer-facing report of soil health with nutrient and soil-amendment advice based on the tested sample. Farmers in Tamil Nadu and other states should contact the local agriculture department or authorised soil-testing facility for sampling and report procedures. A Soil Health Card is not proof of a cash entitlement, an actual lab result for this farmer, or evidence that an untested field has a nutrient deficiency. Confirm sampling depth, crop, test method and local recommendations before acting.

bundles.title: PMKSY Har Khet Ko Pani irrigation access official overview
bundles.reviewed_by: SkyView official primary-source existence and purpose review 2026-10-15; current eligibility and application windows require authority verification
bundles.evidence_text: Har Khet Ko Pani is an irrigation component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana. Its programmes include irrigation infrastructure and water-access measures implemented through approved projects and responsible agencies. This national reference is distinct from Per Drop More Crop micro-irrigation assistance and from PM-KUSUM solar pumps. State and district project coverage, current programme continuation, beneficiary selection and application channels must be verified with the responsible department. An irrigation need alone does not establish entitlement to a borewell, pump or grant.
